title: Use accumulated momentum for non-Nesterov Muon updates
author: sylvesterkaczmarek
body:
## Problem

With `nesterov=False`, Muon updates its momentum buffer but then orthogonalizes the raw gradient. Accumulated momentum therefore has no effect on the parameter update. The orthogonalizer also mutates its input when that input is already bfloat16, because the dtype conversion can alias the original tensor.

## Changes

Use the momentum buffer for the non-Nesterov direction. Normalize out of place so the orthogonalization does not overwrite that buffer or a caller's bfloat16 gradient. Preserve the default Nesterov formula, parameter groups, serialization, and distributed update layout.

## Validation

- **29 CPU tests passed**. On unchanged production code, 14 fail and 15 controls pass.
- Independent update calculations cover three successive steps, both momentum modes, float32/bfloat16, tall/wide/square matrices, and zero/three Newton-Schulz iterations.
- Tests also check the retained momentum buffer, unchanged input gradients, direct helper nonmutation, and parameters without gradients.
- Ruff syntax/error checks and `git diff --check` passed. The baseline remains below its 1,500-line limit.

Python 3.12.14, PyTorch 2.14.1 on macOS arm64. No CUDA/distributed execution, compilation benchmark, dataset, model checkpoint, or end-to-end training run was used. No leaderboard improvement is claimed. This branch is independent of the byte-counting correction and the existing rotary fix.

Reproduced against `f5c079314c4877fbb0af378c0abade5a8ca33d3a`.
